extracted.intended_audience: listeners of This American Life; general public and journalists interested in journalistic fact-checking and corrections
extracted.subtask_description: A retraction notice and accompanying coverage describing failures in reporting for a radio/podcast episode and explaining the program's fact‑checking process, why the episode should not have aired, and corrective actions taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fabrications / truthfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting must not contain fabrications — this episode 'contained numerous fabrications.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fabrications are discovered the program cannot 'stand behind the reporting' and must publicly acknowledge the errors; the episode was retracted and the show details the errors and separates fact from fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroboration by primary source required before airing
rubrics_metrics.description: Without Cathy's corroboration of the story, This American Life 'never should have run the story in the first place.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers must obtain and verify corroboration from key primary sources (e.g., an interpreter or eyewitness) before broadcasting first-person claims; the retraction recounts how Marketplace reporter Rob Schmitz tracked down and interviewed Cathy Lee, whose account disputed much of the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honest disclosure by contributors during fact-checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributors must not mislead producers during fact-checking — 'Mike Daisey lied to This American Life during the fact-checking process, telling Ira and our producers that Cathy was not her real name and that she was unreachable.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors must provide truthful information about sources and accessibility; intentional deception during fact-checking undermines the work and is grounds for retraction and further investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and follow a documented fact-checking process
rubrics_metrics.description: This American Life explains its fact-checking process in general and uses it to judge the episode's failings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should have a clear, documented fact-checking procedure and apply it consistently; when process failures occur, explain the process and where it broke down to the audience (the episode includes Ira explaining TAL's fact-checking).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly distinguish journalism from theatrical or anecdotal performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts presented as reportage must be supported by reporting; theatricalized monologues or anecdotes should not be presented as verified fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When performers blend theater and reportage, producers must ensure listeners understand what is claimed as factual versus theatrical embellishment; the show 'ends...separating fact from fiction' and interrogates which parts of Daisey's story are true.

rubrics_metrics.name: When serious errors are found, issue a public correction/retraction and provide documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The program issued a retraction and detailed the errors, provided transcript and press release, and aired reporting that examined the discrepancies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrective actions should include a public retraction notice, full transcript, related reporting (e.g., interviews that track down disputed sources), and links to supporting materials so the public can assess the correction.
